subject: Ledger reconciliation request — partial-path degradation overlap with upstream maintenance
messages:
From: Christopher Townsend <ctownsend@flowgrid.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@flowgrid.com
Date: Tue, Apr 20, 2027 at 8:14 AM PDT
Subject: Discrepancy in April 16–17 availability ledger

Hi Neha,

We reviewed our traffic and billing for the weekend and noticed a discrepancy between FlowGrid's client-side error/latency measurements and the availability ledger posted in the Redwood portal. On 2027-04-16 between ~16:40–17:20 UTC our customers saw a spike in 5xxs and client-side timeouts (roughly 12% of requests for a 40-minute window), but the ledger shows no SLA credit for that period.

Attached are: flowgrid-client-logs.zip (client-side request logs filtered to the impacted window) and a short CSV with synthetic test runs. We ran cross-region tests and saw increased tail latency and occasional request failures. We do run a small set of synthetic probes but these are representative of customer-reported behavior.

Can you check how Redwood attributed availability for that window? If this was a Redwood-side degradation we will request the appropriate invoice credit per the SLA. If the issue aligns with an upstream / third‑party maintenance window, please share your apportionment so we can reconcile.

We’d like to resolve before the invoice posts on May 1. Happy to join a short call if that helps.

Thanks,
Chris Townsend
CTO, FlowGrid
ctownsend@flowgrid.com
Attachments: flowgrid-client-logs.zip (attachment)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Christopher Townsend <ctownsend@flowgrid.com>
Cc: procurement@flowgrid.com, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, Apr 20, 2027 at 9:03 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in April 16–17 availability ledger

Hi Chris — thanks for the logs and the heads up. I’ve opened an internal ticket (INC-4321) to track this and looped in SRE (Ben) and the account team (Stephanie, Marissa).

Preliminary check of our availability ledger shows an upstream maintenance event reported by EdgeCloud between 16:32–17:15 UTC that coincides with much of the window you flagged. We also see a partial-path degradation pattern starting ~16:45 UTC with elevated 95/99 latencies in a subset of our egress nodes.

To move quickly: please confirm the client timestamps are in UTC and provide any additional traces that include request IDs and retry behavior (that helps correlate at token/request granularity). We will:
- Share our probe and node-level logs for the same window
- Run a side-by-side correlation and propose an apportionment for credit (we do not automatically assign full credit if the cause is multi-factor)

Proposed next steps:
1) You share exact UTC timestamps + traces (if possible) — we’ll correlate on our side.
2) We’ll propose an apportionment and a proposed credit amount within 48 hours.
3) If needed, schedule a 30-min joint debug session with engineering.

Do you have availability for a call tomorrow afternoon (US PDT)?

- Neha Kapoor
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Redwood Inference — Production SLA team

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, Apr 21, 2027 at 10:25 AM PDT
Subject: Internal: probe summary & suggested apportionment for INC-4321

Internal notes / analysis (not for external distribution until we confirm):

I pulled probe and node metrics for the 16:20–17:40 UTC range:
- EdgeCloud maintenance window (provider reported): 16:32–17:15 UTC (confirmed via provider bulletin).
- Our probe aggregation shows a sharp latency tail increase starting ~16:45 UTC, peaking around 16:58 UTC, and tapering off by ~17:22 UTC.
- Error rates (5xx) cluster on a subset of egress nodes that share a common upstream path; internal traces indicate repeated timeouts and KV cache misses that increased token generation latency.

Preliminary apportionment guidance: the overlap shows both a provider maintenance and a transient internal partial-path degradation. Given the evidence, I’d recommend Redwood accept responsibility for 30–40% of the impact and attribute the remainder to the upstream maintenance. Rationale: the degradation on our egress path amplified the effect of the provider maintenance (cache invalidation + retry amplification).

Suggested language to customer: offer a 35% credit for the impacted window as a one-time invoice adjustment; include a postmortem and compensating controls (probe tuning, cache priming, and routing policy change).

Attachment: redwood-probe-summary.csv (internal probe aggregates)

- Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Christopher Townsend <ctownsend@flowgrid.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@flowgrid.com, platform-ops@flowgrid.com
Date: Thu, Apr 21, 2027 at 2:02 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in April 16–17 availability ledger

Neha,

Thanks — attaching our server-side traces (flowgrid-server-traces.tar.gz). Timestamps are UTC; we include per-request IDs. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- The customer impact we observed spans multiple regions (US-WEST and EU-CENTRAL) not just a single egress path, which suggests the issue is broader than a single Redwood node.
- FlowGrid did not schedule maintenance and we have no provider bulletin on our side during that window.

We’re open to a split credit if the apportionment is justified by the correlation; however, given multi-region customer impact we (and our procurement team) expect a conservative approach to apportionment. If Redwood intends to apportion, please share the method and the math so we can reconcile.

Availability for a call: tomorrow morning (PDT) works for Chris and the platform team.

Chris Townsend
CTO, FlowGrid
Attachments: flowgrid-server-traces.tar.gz (attachment)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Christopher Townsend <ctownsend@flowgrid.com>
Cc: procurement@flowgrid.com, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, Apr 22, 2027 at 3:30 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in April 16–17 availability ledger — proposed resolution

Chris / FlowGrid team — thanks for the fast turnaround and for the traces. We completed a side-by-side correlation (see INC-4321) and reviewed internal probe aggregates. Summary and proposal:

Findings (short):
- EdgeCloud reported a maintenance event 16:32–17:15 UTC that coincides with a majority of the impacted timeframe.
- Our node-level traces show partial-path degradation starting ~16:45 UTC that amplified client-visible errors (retries and KV cache misses increased).
- FlowGrid traces confirm customer impact across regions, which explains the broader visibility on your side despite the upstream maintenance being regionally focused.

Proposed resolution:
- Redwood will offer a one-time invoice adjustment equal to 35% of the token charges for the impacted window (apportioned credit).
- We will provide a short postmortem that includes: timeline, root cause analysis, and three mitigations (probe tuning, cache priming, and routing policy change).
- Schedule a 30-min joint review next week to walk through the traces and the postmortem.

If FlowGrid accepts the 35% apportionment we will issue the credit against the May invoice and share the postmortem within 5 business days. If you prefer a different split, let us know with the math and we’ll re-run the reconciliation.

Attachments: resolution-proposal.pdf
Related ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4321

Appreciate the collaboration here — we want to make sure the accounting is fair and transparent.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
